scope: Public programme preview only. Complete lessons must be served after payment entitlement verification.

lessons.title: Understand AI without the hype
lessons.objective: Explain generative AI, strengths, limitations, hallucinations and when human review is necessary.
lessons.exercise: Compare an AI answer with a trustworthy source and mark three claims requiring verification.
lessons.deliverable: A one-page AI opportunity and risk map
lessons.check: Identify two common AI failure modes

lessons.title: Choose a useful problem
lessons.objective: Define a specific user, task, source material, desired result and success criteria.
lessons.exercise: Turn a vague ambition into a measurable task brief.
lessons.check: Select the task that has observable success criteria

lessons.title: Write a prompt that works
lessons.objective: Use goal, audience, context, constraints and output format deliberately.
lessons.exercise: Rewrite three weak prompts and compare the resulting outputs.
lessons.check: Identify missing context in a prompt

lessons.title: Iterate and improve
lessons.objective: Use an iterative cycle: draft, inspect, challenge, revise and accept.
lessons.exercise: Refine an email prompt over three cycles while recording changes.
lessons.check: Choose the strongest revision strategy

lessons.title: Verify before you trust
lessons.objective: Differentiate source-backed claims, citation links, speculation and out-of-date answers.
lessons.exercise: Fact-check a short AI-written guide against two primary sources.
lessons.check: Spot unsupported claims and misleading citations

lessons.title: Protect private information
lessons.objective: Understand personal-data minimisation, confidential files, copyright and safe sharing.
lessons.exercise: Redact a mock customer note before using it in an AI prompt.
lessons.check: Identify what cannot be pasted into a public assistant

lessons.title: Week 1 challenge: useful assistant
lessons.objective: Combine task design, prompting, verification and safe use.
lessons.exercise: Create a reusable assistant prompt for one task, test it, and document limitations.
lessons.check: Rubric: clarity, safety, evidence, usefulness

lessons.title: Write emails people want to read
lessons.objective: Control intent, brevity, tone, audience and calls to action.
lessons.exercise: Create three email variants for one situation and select the best.
lessons.check: Identify a weak or missing call to action

lessons.title: Summarise accurately
lessons.objective: Distinguish extracting facts from adding interpretation and use source-grounded summaries.
lessons.exercise: Summarise supplied notes into a 100-word brief with no new facts.
lessons.check: Detect invented summary details

lessons.title: Research with a source trail
lessons.objective: Ask answerable questions, compare sources and keep a verification trail.
lessons.exercise: Prepare a three-source research brief; flag source age and conflicts.
lessons.deliverable: Research memo with links and caveats
lessons.check: Choose the most authoritative evidence

lessons.title: Work with spreadsheets
lessons.objective: Describe data columns, ask for checks, and validate calculations independently.
lessons.exercise: Clean a sample sales table and calculate totals using formulas.
lessons.check: Catch a formula error in a sample report

lessons.title: Draft a business proposal
lessons.objective: Structure an executive summary, problem, options, plan, assumptions and risks.
lessons.exercise: Create a concise proposal from a supplied scenario.
lessons.check: Find unsupported ROI claims

lessons.title: Prepare a presentation
lessons.objective: Build a narrative, concise slide outline and accurate visual brief.
lessons.exercise: Plan a seven-slide presentation with speaker notes.
lessons.check: Choose a logically ordered slide sequence

lessons.title: Week 2 challenge: work pack
lessons.objective: Combine research, writing, analysis and presentation into one coherent deliverable.
lessons.exercise: Deliver a source-checked briefing, email and mini-presentation.
lessons.check: Rubric: completeness, accuracy, clarity, accessibility

lessons.title: Understand your audience
lessons.objective: Distinguish evidence-based customer insights from invented personas.
lessons.exercise: Build a research-backed audience hypothesis for a product.
lessons.check: Separate facts, assumptions and experiments

lessons.title: Write persuasive marketing copy
lessons.objective: Use truthful value propositions, proof and responsible calls to action.
lessons.exercise: Create website hero and three advert variations without false claims.
lessons.check: Spot an unsupported marketing claim

lessons.title: Plan social content
lessons.objective: Create themed content pillars, cadence and consistent brand voice.
lessons.exercise: Build a seven-day content plan with captions and CTAs.
lessons.check: Match content with the audience objective

lessons.title: Design better graphics
lessons.objective: Use composition, contrast, brand rules, accessible typography and visual hierarchy.
lessons.exercise: Create an original promotional graphic with readable mobile text.
lessons.check: Assess readability and hierarchy

lessons.title: Prompt for images responsibly
lessons.objective: Write an image brief with subject, style, composition, lighting and exclusions.
lessons.exercise: Generate or brief three original images and evaluate fidelity and rights.
lessons.check: Identify misleading or rights-infringing use

lessons.title: Storyboard a short video
lessons.objective: Develop a hook, problem, demonstration, proof and call to action.
lessons.exercise: Create a 20-second original ad storyboard with shot and caption timing.
lessons.check: Spot a misleading result claim

lessons.title: Week 3 challenge: campaign kit
lessons.objective: Combine audience evidence, copy, design and channel planning.
lessons.exercise: Assemble a one-week campaign and critique it against a brand checklist.
lessons.check: Rubric: truthful, cohesive, usable, accessible

lessons.title: Break tasks into repeatable steps
lessons.objective: Map triggers, inputs, decisions, human approval and outputs.
lessons.exercise: Turn one manual workflow into a clear process map.
lessons.check: Identify missing review and exception branches

lessons.title: Build a reusable prompt library
lessons.objective: Create templates with variables, constraints and acceptance tests.
lessons.exercise: Build and test five prompts for real business or work tasks.
lessons.check: Choose the prompt with complete safeguards

lessons.title: Compare multiple AI tools
lessons.objective: Choose tools based on verified current capabilities, privacy, output and cost.
lessons.exercise: Score four tools for one scenario using an evidence table.
lessons.check: Distinguish verified capability from marketing claims

lessons.title: Automate carefully
lessons.objective: Understand trigger-action flows, permissions, retries, audit logging and consent.
lessons.exercise: Design a test-only reminder workflow with human approval.
lessons.check: Identify an unsafe unattended action

lessons.title: Improve outputs with rubrics
lessons.objective: Use evaluation criteria, counterexamples and human judgement; avoid blind self-scoring.
lessons.exercise: Evaluate two drafts with a weighted rubric and revise one.
lessons.check: Find a rubric that is measurable and fair

lessons.title: Measure impact
lessons.objective: Set baseline, time saved, error rate and quality metrics without inventing ROI.
lessons.exercise: Calculate a hypothetical before/after productivity example and note assumptions.
lessons.check: Distinguish gross savings from verified profit

lessons.title: Capstone: ship one useful workflow
lessons.objective: Integrate planning, safe prompting, source-checking, output design and measurement.
lessons.exercise: Produce and demonstrate a complete, repeatable AI-powered workflow.
lessons.deliverable: Final working project, portfolio case study and reflection
lessons.check: Rubric: 80% threshold; human-reviewed evidence and resubmission
